rulings.challenge_claim: Two challenges on the single-verse row at Jer.4.10. (a) A rare reach/touch verb brackets Jer.4.10 with Jer.4.18 as an undisclosed cross-seam catchword although the row asserts its disclosure needs are already complete. (b) The row's 'bracketed by third-person material on both sides' overreaches: a three-word addressee run carries straight across the back seam into Jer.4.11, and the material turns to divine first person two verses on.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one. (b) UPHELD in full. The addressee run לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם stands at oshb:Jer.4.10 (byte tier) and recurs as לָֽעָם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier); one consonantal skeleton underlies both spellings and that skeleton stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide - these two and no others (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys). It sits on this row's own back seam, and the pairing is not merely lexical: the reported assurance closes on לֵאמֹ֔ר (oshb:Jer.4.10, byte tier) and the passive יֵאָמֵ֤ר heads oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier), so the following verse inverts the very speech-act protested here. The bracketing characterisation is byte-false on the following side: לִזְר֖וֹת וְל֥וֹא stands at oshb:Jer.4.11 and גַּם אֲנִ֛י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר at oshb:Jer.4.12 (byte tier), divine first person within two verses of the seam. (a) REFINED - the digit survives, the framing does not. A contiguous consonantal sweep of the three-letter string returns 5 verses (sweep: 5 verses, MT keys: 4:10, 4:18, 12:14, 48:32, 51:9), so 'five verses' is a substring figure, not a token or form census; token-bound the bare form נָגַ֖ע stands at 2 verses (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys: 4:18, 51:9) and Jer.4.10 carries the different, vav-prefixed וְנָגְעָ֥ה. The two ends lie eight verses apart with two complete units between them, so this is a long-range catchword, not a device straddling this row's own seam. The tight English parity the item leans on is not carried by the Hebrew either: the nouns differ, הַנָּֽפֶשׁ at oshb:Jer.4.10 against לִבֵּֽךְ at oshb:Jer.4.18 (byte tier at each site). NEW FINDING: device_notes makes an UNSCOPED completeness claim while the seg inventory records 1 paseq at MT 4:10 (single-witness, count-only; no intra-verse position is sourceable) - undisclosed. The paragraph report itself is accurate: no petuchah and no setumah at MT 4:9 or MT 4:10 (tier-3 weak, single-witness; absence is not counterevidence). Boundary untouched: the verse-initial speech-attribution turn וָאֹמַ֞ר (oshb:Jer.4.10, byte tier) is a sound onset.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes for Jer.4.10-Jer.4.10, replace the completeness sentence with two disclosures: (i) the seam-sharing addressee run and the speech-verb inversion shared with Jer.4.11, cited at oshb:Jer.4.10 and oshb:Jer.4.11 at byte tier with the swept object named and the 2-verse digit carried; (ii) the 1 paseq seg recorded at MT 4:10, single-witness and count-only, with no intra-verse position asserted. In strongest_rejected_alternative, delete 'bracketed by third-person material on both sides' and state instead the byte-true fact that the following material turns to divine first person by Jer.4.12. Add web:Jer.4.11 and web:Jer.4.12 to boundary_evidence_refs. This is one half of a SEAM-PAIR cure with the Jer.4.11-Jer.4.13 row: both device_notes take the same device in ONE edit, stated once from each side. Do NOT import the reach-verb link as a seam device; if it is mentioned at all it must be labelled a long-range catchword with the form named per site and the substring figure kept apart from the token figure. Tests the cure must pass: span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry over MT 4:10 including the paseq layer; the cross-seam cohesion arm at the Jer.4.10|Jer.4.11 seam, which must now find the device disclosed; the refs-mirror arm over every verse newly argued outside the span.

rulings.challenge_claim: The distinctness argument for Jer.4.11-Jer.4.13 rests on contrast with Jer.4.10 and cites that verse as evidence, yet omits that the two verses carry both of the book's attestations of a three-word addressee run, each governed by a form of the same speech verb - presenting the seam as cleaner than the bytes make it.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on bytes. לָֽעָם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier) answers לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם at oshb:Jer.4.10 (byte tier); one consonantal skeleton underlies both and stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide, this adjacent pair and nowhere else (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys). The governing verbs bind them: לֵאמֹ֔ר closes the preceding report and יֵאָמֵ֤ר opens this one (both byte tier). boundary_rationale names web:Jer.4.10 as its contrast term and states no shared material, so the cited contrast is presented without the countervailing tie - the cross-seam cohesion standard requires the disclosure whichever way the seam is finally read. The onset itself is byte-true and correctly weighted: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יֵאָמֵ֤ר stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier) and the temporal frame is an attested shape at 7 verses (sweep: 7 verses, MT keys: 3:17, 4:11, 8:1, 31:1, 33:15, 50:4, 50:20) - softer than an imperative, vocative or koh-amar restart, which is exactly why the medium posture is right; the boundary is not endangered by this defect. Paragraph report accurate: no petuchah and no setumah at MT 4:10 through MT 4:13 (tier-3 weak, single-witness; absence is not counterevidence). NEW FINDING, for the record rather than against the row: the seg inventory records 1 paseq at MT 4:13, inside the span and unmentioned - the row's negative statement is expressly scoped to the paragraph layer and is accurate there, so this is an incompleteness of coverage, not a false statement.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes for Jer.4.11-Jer.4.13, add the front-seam disclosure: the addressee run shared with Jer.4.10 and the speech-verb inversion, cited at byte tier at both refs with the swept object named and the 2-verse digit carried; and add the 1 paseq seg at MT 4:13 as single-witness and count-only, no position asserted. This edit is the OTHER half of the seam-pair cure with the Jer.4.10 row and must land in the same pass, so the seam is stated once from each side rather than twice from one. boundary_evidence_refs already carries web:Jer.4.10; no ref change is required. Tests the cure must pass: the cross-seam cohesion arm at Jer.4.10|Jer.4.11 must find the device disclosed from both sides; span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry over MT 4:11-4:13 including the paseq layer.

rulings.challenge_claim: (a) Both challenges: the rejected alternative enumerates why neither Jer.4.29 nor Jer.4.30 opens a fresh unit but is silent on the first-person turn at Jer.4.31, a comparable ground it never names or rules out. (b) One challenge adds: the markedness asserted for the pronoun at Jer.4.30 is attached to the quoted qere when the consonantal divergence belongs to the ketiv the row expressly sets aside.
rulings.grounds: (a) is ONE AND THE SAME defect in both challenges, and it is upheld: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי heads oshb:Jer.4.31 (byte tier), a turn to first-person perception, and strongest_rejected_alternative names only Jer.4.29 and Jer.4.30. Both framings need one correction, which does not disturb the finding: the 'same class of marker' they invoke BLENDS three byte-distinct shapes - a speech-attribution finite verb (וָאֹמַ֞ר at oshb:Jer.4.10, וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי at oshb:Jer.5.4), an exclamatory outcry (מֵעַ֣י מֵעַ֨י at oshb:Jer.4.19) and a vocative to the deity (יְהֹוָ֗ה verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.3), none of them a perception verb; the object must be named per shape before the class carries weight. The supporting cross-seam ties are byte-true: the two-word sequence at oshb:Jer.4.19 and oshb:Jer.4.31 stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:18 = WEB 9:19) and the first-person soul noun token-bound at 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses, MT keys), both sites among them - though the far end lies two units back, making this a long-range tie rather than an adjacent-seam device. (b) UPHELD exactly. The inventory records 1 variant note at MT 4:30, and the source writes the unpointed ketiv ואתי immediately before the pointed qere וְאַ֨תְּ (both source bytes; the pointed qere is byte tier). The divergent member - one final yod - is carried by the KETIV the row sets aside: token-bound that skeleton stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3) against 110 verses for the qere skeleton (sweep: 110 verses, MT keys - homograph-blended, a floor on ordinariness, not a pronoun census). The form the row quotes and calls unusual and marked is the common one, and neither witness marks it as unusual. The onset is sound and uncontested: the subordinated formula shape at oshb:Jer.4.27 is attested at 29 verses (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys) and the frame owner does change across the front seam. Mark handling is complete and correctly typed: setumah at MT 4:26 on the front seam, petuchah at MT 4:31 on the closing verse, types not conflated, single-witness and non-driving both stated, the MT 4:30 note disclosed, and no paseq seg recorded in the span.
rulings.remedy: In strongest_rejected_alternative for Jer.4.27-Jer.4.31, add Jer.4.31 to the enumeration and dispose of it on its own bytes, naming the shape exactly - a first-person perception verb after the two-word voice sequence, NOT a speech-attribution formula - and stating why it does not open a fresh unit inside a formula-opened oracle. In boundary_rationale, re-attach the markedness sentence to the ketiv: state that the note's consonantal divergence is carried by the unpointed ketiv, that the pointed qere the splice quotes is the ordinary form, and strike 'unusual, marked'. If the long-range tie to Jer.4.19 is argued in prose, add web:Jer.4.19 to boundary_evidence_refs. PROPOSAL ONLY, explicitly NOT author work: a cut at Jer.4.31 separating the death-cry from the formula-opened oracle is flagged for boss adoption and must not be executed inside this remedy. Tests the cure must pass: the ketiv/qere claim-validation arm must find the markedness attached to the ketiv; the refs-mirror arm over every verse newly argued outside the span; and the rejected alternative must survive the very silence that killed the original - no interior verse meeting the row's own stated onset criterion may be left unruled.

rulings.challenge_claim: The single-verse cut at Jer.5.3 stands on the bytes, but the English gloss offered for its splice drops the very vocative the argument rests on, and the front seam separates two of the book's four sites of the faithfulness noun without disclosing the link.
rulings.grounds: Both items upheld. First: the splice runs four words from the verse head, יְהֹוָ֗ה עֵינֶיךָ֮ הֲל֣וֹא לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ (oshb:Jer.5.3, byte tier), opening on the vocative, while the curly-quoted English in the same field covers only the interrogative that follows; the staged reading carries the vocative first (web:Jer.5.3). The English is a verbatim substring of the staged verse, so the verbatim arm is satisfied and the failure is one of EXTENT - gloss extent must equal splice extent, and the unglossed head is precisely the element the boundary claim is built on. Second: לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ at oshb:Jer.5.3 answers אֱמוּנָ֑ה at oshb:Jer.5.1 (byte tier at each site); on a contiguous consonantal sweep that string stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3), two of them the verses on either side of this front seam. boundary_evidence_refs does carry web:Jer.5.1-Jer.5.2, so the ref is present and only the link is unstated - a disclosure gap, not a missing citation. Severity holds at low: the frame-owner change at the seam is explicit in the bytes (יְהֹוָ֗ה verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.3 against וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי at oshb:Jer.5.4, byte tier), the cut itself is not in question, and the disclosure sentence is otherwise true - the inventory records no paragraph mark, no variant note and no paseq seg at MT 5:3, so the unscoped completeness claim happens to hold at this verse.
rulings.remedy: In boundary_rationale for Jer.5.3-Jer.5.3, re-cut the gloss so it covers the whole four-word splice, taking the staged reading that opens with the vocative, in curly double quotes with the inline web: ref in the same field. Add one sentence disclosing the faithfulness-noun tie across the front seam, naming the swept object, the tier, and the sweep digit with its dual qualifier on the in-zone site. Tests the cure must pass: the gloss-extent parity check that failed here - splice extent equals gloss extent on every Hebrew citation in the row; the WEB-verbatim arm on the re-cut quote; and the cross-seam cohesion arm at the Jer.5.2|Jer.5.3 seam.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset at Jer.5.4 is byte-sound, but a pardon-verb catchword straddling the row's own front seam is undisclosed, the closing refrain is asserted with neither its sites nor a tier named, and the opening splice is glossed at its tail alone.
rulings.grounds: Upheld, with one supporting digit's OBJECT corrected and one sub-item's severity raised. The catchword is byte-true: וְאֶסְלַ֖ח לָֽהּ closes oshb:Jer.5.1 and אֶֽסְלַֽח לָ֔ךְ stands at oshb:Jer.5.7 (both byte tier), so the same first-person pardon verb sits on either side of this row's front seam, and Jer.5.1 appears in no boundary_evidence_refs entry - the list carries the span alone. OBJECT CORRECTION: the 4-verse figure offered for it is a contiguous SUBSTRING figure (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys: 5:1, 5:7, 31:34, 50:20); token-bound the bare form stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys: 5:7, 31:34, 50:20) and EXCLUDES Jer.5.1, whose form is vav-prefixed. The finding survives the correction; the label 'the bare form' does not. Second item upheld: the closing colon is called the refrain with no site and no tier, while the object stands at 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys: 5:9, 5:29 and MT 9:8 = WEB 9:9) and the two in-chapter sites are NOT identical - the four-word opening spliced from oshb:Jer.5.9 matches at oshb:Jer.5.29 at tier NONE, and the reciprocal splice matches at oshb:Jer.5.9 at tier NONE, so the divergence (plene against defective negative, vav-prefixed against bare conditional) survives even at skeleton; only the closing soul-noun tail is byte-shared at both sites. Third: the item filed as minor is RAISED. The opening splice וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי אַךְ דַּלִּ֖ים הֵ֑ם runs five words from the verse head (oshb:Jer.5.4, byte tier) and the curly-quoted English covers only its last three, so the two words the boundary claim rests on - the first-person speech-attribution formula itself - go unglossed; that is the same extent failure recorded at Jer.5.3, not a stylistic nicety. Sound and uncontested: the inventory records variant notes at MT 5:6 and MT 5:7, both disclosed, the source writing the unpointed ketiv immediately before the pointed qere at MT 5:7, which the splice quotes; setumah at MT 5:9 disclosed, correctly typed, single-witness and non-driving; no paseq seg in span. The closure tag at MT 5:9 does sit mid-verse rather than verse-final, but a fresh discourse imperative opens oshb:Jer.5.10, so treating it as closure corroboration is within the ruled weight.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes for Jer.5.4-Jer.5.9, disclose the pardon-verb tie across the front seam, naming the object per attested form (vav-prefixed at Jer.5.1, bare at Jer.5.7), the tier, and a TOKEN-BOUND digit - not the substring digit. In boundary_rationale, re-cut the opening gloss to cover the full five-word splice including the speech-attribution formula; and replace the bare phrase 'the refrain' with a sited, tiered recurrence statement naming the two in-chapter sites plus the third under its dual qualifier, and stating that the sites are not identical at byte, accent-stripped or skeleton tier, only the closing tail being byte-shared. Add web:Jer.5.1 and web:Jer.5.29 to boundary_evidence_refs for the verses newly argued outside the span. Tests the cure must pass: gloss extent equals splice extent on every Hebrew citation in the row; the recurrence-claim arm - a definite-article recurrence claim carries a digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit, and a tier label never substitutes for it; the cross-seam cohesion arm at Jer.5.3|Jer.5.4; the refs-mirror arm over the newly argued verses.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row files a 4-verse divine-title object under the 50-verse one its own bytes exclude it from, leaves the make-a-full-end catchword crossing its front seam undisclosed, and opens its splice on a backward-pointing connective the restart characterisation never engages.
rulings.grounds: The first two items are upheld exactly; the third is refined. First: the bytes at the head of the splice read יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.5.14, byte tier) - the God-of-Armies stack, whose formula collocation stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys: 5:14, 35:17, 38:17, 44:7). observed_substrate_signals records the plain armies-title key instead; as a speech formula that collocation stands at 50 verses (sweep: 50 verses, MT keys) and BYTE-EXCLUDES Jer.5.14, because the intervening אֱלֹהֵ֣י breaks it - and the plain form is exactly what the bytes carry two units later, יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת at oshb:Jer.6.6 (byte tier), which is in the 50. Divine-name objects are each their own count object and are never blended, so one signal key standing for two byte-distinct titles is a mislabelled signal, not a wording preference. Second: the row names the not-a-full-end qualifier in English at Jer.5.18-Jer.5.19 while its Hebrew twin sits across its own front seam - וְכָלָ֖ה אַֽל תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ at oshb:Jer.5.10 against לֹֽא אֶעֱשֶׂ֥ה אִתְּכֶ֖ם כָּלָֽה at oshb:Jer.5.18 (byte tier; bound collocations, sweep: 1 verse each, MT keys - the bare noun is a homograph set at 34 verses and carries no motif digit) - and a third site two units earlier at oshb:Jer.4.27 receives the same English phrase in the staged text. Undisclosed on every side. Third, REFINED: the splice does open on לָכֵ֗ן, a backward-pointing connective, but the connective-plus-formula shape is itself an attested onset shape at 27 verses (sweep: 27 verses, MT keys), so it does not weaken the seam - what the row owes is engagement with the word it quotes, not a different verdict. The seam is sound and uncontested: the formula is divine-mouthed and the frame owner changes from the quoted denial at oshb:Jer.5.12 to divine speech. Setumah at MT 5:13 (front seam) and MT 5:19 (own close) disclosed under the right type, single-witness and non-driving; the inventory records no variant note in span. NEW FINDING: the seg inventory records 1 paseq at MT 5:15, inside the span and unmentioned (single-witness, count-only; no intra-verse position sourceable).
rulings.remedy: In observed_substrate_signals for Jer.5.14-Jer.5.19, replace the plain armies-title key with a key naming the title the bytes actually carry, and keep the two objects apart wherever else the corpus files them under one key - carry that separation as its OWN corpus-wide sweep, not a single-row edit. In device_notes, disclose the make-a-full-end collocation crossing the front seam, naming the bound collocation per site with its 1-verse digit and tier and noting the third site that shares the English phrase, and add the 1 paseq seg at MT 5:15 as single-witness and count-only, no position asserted. In boundary_rationale, engage the connective the splice quotes: state that the shape is connective-plus-formula and that it is an attested onset shape carrying the 27-verse digit, rather than leaving 'restarts' to carry it unaided. Add the out-of-span verses newly argued in prose to boundary_evidence_refs. Tests the cure must pass: the substrate-signal key must survive a byte check that the named title collocation is present in the span; the cross-seam cohesion arm at Jer.5.13|Jer.5.14; span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry over MT 5:14-5:19 INCLUDING the paseq layer; the refs-mirror arm.

rulings.challenge_claim: Both challenges: the declared false-positive disposition on the Jer.5.24 ketiv/qere is refuted - the row quotes out of a verse carrying a variant note with no ketiv/qere disclosure in any field, a real disclosure gap rather than a heuristic artifact. One challenge adds: the row's own onset criterion is met unaddressed inside its span at Jer.5.21, and the declare-and-publish echo carries neither digit nor tier.
rulings.grounds: The ketiv/qere item is the SAME defect in both challenges and is upheld; the declared disposition is refuted on bytes. The inventory records 1 variant note at MT 5:24, inside this span, and the source writes the unpointed ketiv immediately before the pointed qere, וירה יוֹרֶ֥ה (source bytes), inside the very clause the row's second illustration is drawn from; no field of the row mentions a ketiv, a qere or a variant note. The asymmetry is decisive against 'inert': notes are disclosed at MT 5:6, MT 5:7 and MT 6:7 in the units flanking this one, so no row-level convention covers the omission. ONE CORRECTION to the supporting characterisation: the note does not ride on the words the row quotes - the row's curly-quoted English is the season phrase, rendering בְּעִתּ֑וֹ (oshb:Jer.5.24, byte tier), while the note rides on the early-rain noun one word earlier in the same clause. The disclosure is owed because the SPAN touches the note and the quoted clause contains it, not because the noted word is itself quoted. Second item upheld: שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם heads oshb:Jer.5.21 (byte tier), an imperative with a vocative in the same clause - the device class the row treats as onset-making at Jer.5.20 - and no field rules it out. The byte that subordinates it, בִיהוּדָ֖ה closing oshb:Jer.5.20 (byte tier), is the word the row's own splice stops immediately before, and the staged translation opens its inner quotation there; so the answer is available and unstated. That is an argument gap, not a boundary error. Third item upheld: the declare-and-publish echo is asserted with neither digit nor tier while the pairing stands at 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys: 4:5, 5:20, 46:14, 50:2) and the two forms differ - הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ at Jer.4.5 against the vav-prefixed, suffixed וְהַשְׁמִיע֥וּהָ at Jer.5.20, which stands at 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse, MT keys). Sound and uncontested: the refusal to cut where the receiving translation closes a quotation mark correctly treats that as tier-4 apparatus and not a Hebrew seam; setumah at MT 5:19 disclosed on the front seam, single-witness and non-driving; the inventory records no other paragraph mark and no paseq seg in the span. For the record only: the cited echo source at Jer.4.5 itself carries a variant note, though the span-relevant standard does not reach outside the span.
rulings.remedy: In device_notes for Jer.5.20-Jer.5.24, add the ketiv/qere disclosure for MT 5:24 - single-witness, named as a variant note, with no reconstruction of the unpointed reading beyond the source bytes - and treat the declared false-positive disposition on this warning as REFUTED: it must not be re-declared. In strongest_rejected_alternative, add Jer.5.21 and rule it out: state that its imperative-plus-vocative is subordinated by the speech-verb closing Jer.5.20, and extend the boundary_rationale splice through that word so the quotation carries its own answer. In boundary_rationale, give the declare-and-publish echo a digit and a tier and name the two forms as distinct spellings rather than one repetition. Tests the cure must pass: the ketiv/qere-quote arm that raised the original warning must clear on the row as edited; the recurrence-claim arm - every echo claim carries a digit-bearing sweep naming the swept object and unit; and the rejected alternative must dispose of EVERY interior verse meeting the row's own stated onset criterion, which is the silence that killed the original.

rulings.challenge_claim: The onset survives, but the cited echo is attributed to the wrong verse - the one other verse carrying the northern colon of Jer.6.1 is Jer.4.6, not Jer.4.5 - and the ground given for holding Jer.6.2 with Jer.6.3 is contradicted by both witnesses.
rulings.grounds: The second defect is upheld in full; the headline framing of the first needs correcting. UPHELD: strongest_rejected_alternative holds Jer.6.2 with Jer.6.3 on the ground that both continue in the same third-person descriptive mode, but the finite verb of oshb:Jer.6.2 is דָּמִ֖יתִי (byte tier), carrying the first-person singular suffix, and the staged English reads it as first person as well; the third-person material is Jer.6.3's shepherds. Half the span that sentence defends is misdescribed, and the misdescription sits in the field carrying the row's rival disclosure. The seam is nevertheless undisturbed: neither Jer.6.2 nor Jer.6.3 carries an imperative, a vocative or a speech formula, so the pronominal turn is not a tier-1 onset and the unit holds as cut. REFINED: the echo is NOT attributed to a wrong verse. The collocation תִּקְע֣וּ שׁוֹפָ֔ר is byte-true at both oshb:Jer.4.5 and oshb:Jer.6.1 and stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys: 4:5, 6:1, 51:27), so the cited echo exists - it is simply absent from the run the row splices, which shares no consonantal token with Jer.4.5, and it is not exclusive. What is genuinely undisclosed is a STRONGER twin: the colon מִצָּפ֖וֹן וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל, spliced from oshb:Jer.4.6, matches at oshb:Jer.6.1 at BYTE tier, and that string stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys: 4:6, 6:1); the opening imperative is a mater-lectionis pair with the same verse - plene הָעִ֖יזוּ at oshb:Jer.4.6 against defective הָעִ֣זוּ at oshb:Jer.6.1, 1 verse per spelling (sweep: 1 verse each, MT keys), the book's only two occurrences. Jer.4.6 appears in no boundary_evidence_refs entry while the row's own quoted continuation is the material that duplicates it. The onset needs no echo at all: the verse-initial imperative with a vocative in the same clause is a sufficient warrant on its own bytes. Paragraph report accurate - no petuchah and no setumah at MT 5:31 or within MT 6:1-6:3 (tier-3 weak, single-witness; absence is not counterevidence) - and the seg inventory records 1 paseq at MT 6:1, unmentioned, though the row's negative statement is scoped to the paragraph layer and is true there.
